summary: Today’s pulse tracks Lindsay Clancy's lawyer now questions whether she killed her 3 children, Jack Smith says Lindsey Graham would ‘likely’ have been a witness in case against Trump – US politics live, and New York Times executive fatally shot by elderly in-laws, police say. Across NPR, Guardian, BBC, and Ars Technica, the strongest repeated signals are burnham, trump, and first. In the background, Apple worked with Trump admin to remove ICE-tracking apps, lawmaker says and Burnham says he would put PR in Labour manifesto and scrap triple lock to fund social care – UK politics live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Lindsay Clancy's lawyer now questions whether she killed her 3 children
headlines.description: Lindsay Clancy's lawyer is arguing that there wasn't enough evidence to prove she killed her three children. It's a striking turn after a lengthy trial that focused more on her mental state than on whether she took their lives.

headlines.title: Jack Smith says Lindsey Graham would ‘likely’ have been a witness in case against Trump – US politics live
headlines.description: Republican senator Darline Graham accuses former special counsel of adding ‘stress’ to her brother’s life through subpoenas but Smith says he was ‘a patriot’ Sign up to the US Breaking News email For some context, it’s worth remembering that Smith had a two-volume report of his findings as a result of his criminal investigations – that resulted in two indictments against the president after his first term. The first focused on Donald Trump’s attempts to overturn the 2020 election, while the second on the president’s retention of classified documents. However, in February, a Trump-appointed federal judge permanently barred the justice department from releasing the second volume of Smith’s report .

headlines.title: New York Times executive fatally shot by elderly in-laws, police say
headlines.description: Jonathan McKinsey's in-laws, who are both 77 years old, face multiple charges including first-degree murder.

headlines.title: Apple worked with Trump admin to remove ICE-tracking apps, lawmaker says
headlines.description: Lawmaker rejects Apple excuse for banning ICE-tracking apps as unconstitutional.

headlines.title: Burnham says he would put PR in Labour manifesto and scrap triple lock to fund social care – UK politics live
headlines.description: PM, in first speech to party conference as leader, insists his plans are a ‘good deal’ for older people Burnham to signal willingness to look at scrapping pension triple lock to fund social care Angela Rayner , the housing secretary, has apparently confirmed that Andy Burnham will float the prospect of getting rid of the pensions triple lock to help fund the creation of an NHS-style care service. Asked about the prospect on Sky’s Electoral Dysfunction podcast, Rayner said that Burnham was “absolutely right to start the conversation” and that he was being “brave”. The high principle on this is that people have paid in all their lives. They are willing, I think, to look at that. What they don’t want is what they consider to be, quite frankly, incompetent politicians that are going to take something from us to fill a black hole. When we met with Andy [Burnham] this week, it certainly wasn’t mentioned. But I do think that it’s important that Labour make sure that working-class people know that they’re on their side, and this would be a direction of travel that would say the opposite to that. What I understood the national care service to be was a universal benefit: everybody paid in and everybody gets out, and that is what actually the principle of that is. Going to a group of people who are getting around £12,500 a year in order to pay for it to take away their security is wrong.

headlinePool.title: Burnham’s emotional solo act had Labour in raptures – but his promises will take time to come good
headlinePool.description: PM’s speech, written almost entirely alone, was full of radicalism but his biggest plans will have to wait until after the next election Key takeaways from Andy Burnham’s conference speech UK politics live – latest updates Hope Again is the conference slogan. But what felt even more apt was Try Again. Just forget about the last two years, after the party won a historic majority but where the mood never matched the achievement. Now, as conference delegates and MPs filed out of the hall after Andy Burnham’s first speech as prime minister , it was close to euphoria. Where the hell have you been all our lives? What have we been doing – when you were right there all along?

headlinePool.title: Barclays softens return-to-office plans for UK staff after backlash
headlinePool.description: Bank allows employees to delay being in workplace at least three days a week until 2027, if permission granted Barclays has watered down its return-to-office plans after a major staff backlash , with the bank allowing some employees to wait until next year before having to be in at least three days a week. The bank this summer announced the attendance requirement would come in for its 45,000 UK staff from 5 October, with more senior employees expected to come in for at least four days. That compares with current rules requiring staff to come in for two. automatic exemptions of in-office attendance rules during school holidays and Christmas; capping in-office requirements at one day a week for any carers or people with disabilities; flexible start and finish times to allow for cheaper off-peak travel costs and to accommodate school pickup and drop-offs; subsidised onsite meal costs; and a single, consolidated payment made to all staff to make up for the costs of coming into the office, before March 2027.

headlinePool.title: This startup wants to prove gene-editing embryos is safe for making healthy babies
headlinePool.description: Origin Genomics aims to prove that the potential benefits of its technology for editing disease-causing genes in human embryos outweigh the risks.

headlinePool.title: CDC reports second measles death in US while excluding Pennsylvania deaths
headlinePool.description: Pennsylvania has reported over 900 measles cases and four deaths as governor and health chief RFK Jr spar over data A second measles death in the US has been announced on Tuesday by the federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), as the country grapples with an outbreak affecting 47 states. As of 24 September, a total of 3,659 measles cases have been confirmed by the CDC, with the two deaths having been confirmed on Tuesday. The confirmation did not specify in which states the deaths had occurred.

headlinePool.title: Eiffel Tower chief to quit after female staff replaced by men during religious visit
headlinePool.description: The company that runs the Eiffel Tower said the removal of female staff during the visit earlier this month was "unacceptable".

headlinePool.title: Saudi Arabia urged to reconcile with UAE to drive back Houthi separatists in Yemen
headlinePool.description: Relations between the two countries soured in January when a UAE-backed force was defeated by Saudi Arabia in Yemen Saudi Arabia is being urged to reconcile with the United Arab Emirates over Yemen as the price Riyadh must pay to form a military alliance capable of driving the Houthis back. Relations between the UAE and Saudi Arabia in Yemen, where both had backed anti-Houthi forces, plummeted in January this year when a force with which it had been aligned – the separatist Southern Transitional Council (STC) – was attacked and defeated by Saudi Arabia in a move intended to squash its attempt to recreate a separate southern state. The UAE subsequently effectively quit Yemen.

headlinePool.title: Team of skydivers drop in to help survivors of a plane crash in Wisconsin
headlinePool.description: Recreational jumpers used their training as paramedics to treat crash victims before ground crews arrived A team of experienced skydivers recently dropped in to help at a plane crash they happened to witness in Wisconsin – and used their training as paramedics to treat a seriously injured victim before ground-based rescue crews arrived. The single-engine plane carrying four people crashed in a cornfield near East Troy on Sunday, watched by the occupants of a Skydive Milwaukee aircraft who were preparing for an afternoon of recreational jumping.
